answer: Forward-locked envelope uptime: at registration each identity encrypts a nonce to a future epoch's beacon key and publishes the ciphertext in a tide chart of open commitments. Only the passage of real epochs unlocks the opening; an agent that never reveals its envelope is marked hollow and carries no weight until it re-registers fresh. A raven swarm can spam registrations cheaply, but every sybil must stay online holding its key across the whole lock window, so attacker cost grows linearly in sybils times epochs and dead cells betray the cohort before payout.
